newsitem.title: USA: SWIMMING-CARVIN PUTS HEART PROBLEMS ASIDE TO WIN FOUR TITLES.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-CARVIN PUTS HEART PROBLEMS ASIDE TO WIN FOUR TITLES.

text.p: Chad Carvin, in his first major meet since contracting a heart virus, on Sunday became the second man since Mark Spitz in 1972 to win four U.S. titles in one national championship.
Carvin, 22, won his fourth national title in the 1500-meter freestyle Sunday in 15 minutes, 29.44 seconds on the final day of the U.S. National Swimming Championships.
Earlier in the week, Carvin won the 200-meter freestyle and 400-meter individual medley back-to-back and the 800-meter freestyle.
The other U.S. swimmer to win four in one meet was Tom Dolan at the 1994 spring nationals.
"That was the hardest race of the meet for me. I haven't swam a hard mile for two years," Carvin said. "There are parts to that race where you just want to start and cry it hurts so bad."
Carvin was competing in his first major meet since being sidelined for nearly a year with cardiomyopathy, a virus of the heart muscle.

Considered certain to make the Olympic team, Carvin was diagnosed with the severe ailment in December 1995 and missed the March 1996 Olympic Trials. He must take heart medication for the rest of his life.
"Some nights while I've been here, I try to think back a year ago, and what I was thinking about and the way I was feeling," Carvin said. "It is just amazing how far you can come in a year."

Other winners Sunday, the fifth and final night of the first major U.S. swim meet since the Olympics in Atlanta last summer included Olympic gold medalist Brooke Bennett, who swam a lifetime best in the 1500-meter freestyle in 16:13.89, making her the sixth fastest American ever in the event. She swept the middle and distance events, winning the 400-and 800-meter freestyle.
Two-time Olympian Jenny Thompson and Bill Pilczuk won the 50-meter freestyle titles. It was Thompson's 17th national title, the most career titles by any active swimmer.
She won in 25.52. Pilczuk, the 1995 Pan American Games silver medalist, won in the event, won in 22.92.
Jennifer Parmenter swept the individual medley events for the third time at a U.S. nationals in two years. Parmenter won the 200 IM in 2:15.97. She won the 400 IM Friday.
Ron Karnaugh, at 30, the oldest male in the meet, won the 200 IM in 2:03.43.
